arxiv-1705-08047.title: On nonhomogeneous elliptic equations with
arxiv-1705-08047.description: Abstract In this paper, we present some suitable distributional identities of solutions for nonhomogeneous elliptic equations involving the Hardy-Leray potentials and study qualitative properties of the solutions to the corresponding nonhomogeneous problems in this distributional sense. We address some applications on the nonexistence of some nonhomogeneous problems with the Hardy-Leray potentials and the nonexistence principle eigenvalue with some indefinite potentials.

arxiv-2109-10229.title: Adoption and Actual Privacy of Decentralized CoinJoin Implementations in Bitcoin Conference: 4th ACM Conference on Advances in Financial Technologies; September 19–21, 2022; San Francisco, CA, USA 4th ACM Conference on Advances in Financial Technologies (AFT ’22), September 19–21, 2022, San Francisc
arxiv-2109-10229.creator: Rainer Stütz, Johann Stockinger, Pedro Moreno-Sanchez, Bernhard Haslhofer, Matteo Maffei
arxiv-2109-10229.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Rainer Stütz, Johann Stockinger, Pedro Moreno-Sanchez, Bernhard Haslhofer, Matteo Maffei. We present a first measurement study on the adoption and actual privacy of two popular decentralized CoinJoin implementations, Wasabi and Samourai, in the broader Bitcoin ecosystem.

arxiv-2401-04607.title: The directed Cayley diameter and the Davenport constant Thanks: Partially supported by the Hungarian National Research, Development and Innovation Office, NKFIH K 138828, K 132002.
arxiv-2401-04607.creator: Réka András, Kálmán Cziszter, Mátyás Domokos, István Szöllősi
arxiv-2401-04607.description: Abstract . The directed Cayley diameter of a finite group is investigated in terms of the monoid of product-one sequences over the group, via the new notion of directed geodesic atoms. Two quantities associated to the set of directed geodesic atoms provide lower and upper bounds for the directed Cayley diameter.

arxiv-2409-14992.title: A multi-dimensional, robust, and cell-centered finite-volume scheme for the ideal MHD equations
arxiv-2409-14992.creator: Pascal Tremblin, Rémi Bourgeois, Solène Bulteau, Samuel Kokh, Thomas Padioleau, Maxime Delorme, Antoine Strugarek, Matthias González, Allan Sacha Brun
arxiv-2409-14992.description: Abstract We present a new multi-dimensional, robust, and cell-centered finite-volume scheme for the ideal MHD equations. This scheme relies on relaxation and splitting techniques and can be easily used at high order. A fully conservative version is not entropy satisfying but is observed experimentally to be more robust than standard constrained transport schemes at low plasma beta.

arxiv-2501-06006.title: CamCtrl3D: Single-Image Scene Exploration with Precise 3D Camera Control
arxiv-2501-06006.creator: Stefan Popov, Amit Raj, Michael Krainin, Yuanzhen Li, William T. Freeman, Michael Rubinstein
arxiv-2501-06006.description: Abstract We propose a method for generating fly-through videos of a scene, from a single image and a given camera trajectory. We build upon an image-to-video latent diffusion model Blattmann et al. 2023a . We condition its UNet Ronneberger et al. 2015 denoiser on the camera trajectory, using four techniques.

arxiv-2601-21529.title: Fast and Geometrically Grounded Lorentz Neural Networks
arxiv-2601-21529.creator: Robert van der Klis, Ricardo Chávez Torres, Max van Spengler, Yuhui Ding, Thomas Hofmann, Pascal Mettes
arxiv-2601-21529.description: Abstract Hyperbolic space is quickly gaining traction as a promising geometry for hierarchical and robust representation learning. A core open challenge is the development of a mathematical formulation of hyperbolic neural networks that is both efficient and captures the key properties of hyperbolic space.

britannica-1911-omelette.title: Omelette (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-omelette.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-omelette.description: Article 'Omelette' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 20), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. word of which the history is an example of the curious changes a word may undergo. The ultimate origin is Lat. lamella, diminutive of lamina, plate; this became in French lamelle, and a wrong division of la lamelle gave alamelle, alemelle, or alumelle; thence alemette, metathesized to amelette and aumelete, the form in which the word appears in the 15th and 16th centuries.

pmc-11455429.title: 12437 Impact Of Wearable Brain Sensing Meditation Device On Quality Of Life In Patients Recovering From Hypercortisolism Following Surgical Intervention: A Prospective Longitudinal Cohort Study
pmc-11455429.creator: Jasmine Saini, Bahar Bahrani Fard, Malavika Suresh, Rashi Sandooja, Yana Hleibiehova, Elizabeth Atkinson, Sara Achenbach, Irina Bancos
pmc-11455429.description: Disclosure: J. Saini: None. B. Bahrani Fard: None. M. Suresh: None. R. Sandooja: None. Y. Hleibiehova: None. E. Atkinson: None. S. Achenbach: None. I. Bancos: None. Background: Patients with endogenous hypercortisolism experience glucocorticoid withdrawal syndrome (GWS) following curative surgery. The symptoms of GWS include fatigue, weakness, muscle aches, joint pain, mood changes, and sleep disturbance.

pmc-11558568.title: Morphophysiological responses of Theobroma cacao L. rootstocks to flooding and post-flooding conditions
pmc-11558568.creator: M.L.P.B. Pinto, J. Crasque, B. Cerri Neto, T.R. Ferreira, C.A.S. Souza, A.R. Falqueto, T.C. De Souza, J.A. Machado Filho, L.O. Arantes, S. Dousseau-Arantes
pmc-11558568.description: This study investigates how cocoa rootstocks respond to flooding and post-flooding conditions, offering insights for cocoa plantation sustainability in flood-prone areas due to climate change. We studied Theobroma cacao L. rootstocks for 60 d of flooding and 30 d post-flooding, grafting PS-1319 scions onto five rootstocks (TSH-1188, Cepec-2002, Pará, Esfip-02, SJ-02).

pmc-11605088.title: Decoupled responses of plants and soil biota to global change across the world’s land ecosystems
pmc-11605088.creator: Qingshui Yu, Chenqi He, Mark A. Anthony, Bernhard Schmid, Arthur Gessler, Chen Yang, Danhua Zhang, Xiaofeng Ni, Yuhao Feng, Jiangling Zhu, Biao Zhu, Shaopeng Wang, Chengjun Ji, Zhiyao Tang, Jin Wu, Pete Smith, Lingli Liu, Mai-He Li, Marcus Schaub, Jingyun Fang
pmc-11605088.description: Understanding the concurrent responses of aboveground and belowground biota compartments to global changes is crucial for the maintenance of ecosystem functions and biodiversity conservation. We conduct a comprehensive analysis synthesizing data from 13,209 single observations and 3223 pairwise observations from 1166 publications across the world terrestrial ecosystems to examine the responses of plants and soil organisms and their synchronization.

pmc-12558776.title: Integrating proteomics revealed the key targets for molecular breeding of fine cashmere traits in cashmere goats
pmc-12558776.creator: Chongyan Zhang, Yichuan Wang, Anru Xing, Bo Xu, Mingkun Wang, Zhixin Wang, Zhihong Liu
pmc-12558776.description: In this study, the molecular mechanism of superfine fiber properties of Inner Mongolia Alpas cashmere was revealed by using fiber physical properties measurement and deep proteomics technology. The results showed that the average diameter of Alpas cashmere fiber (14.13 μm) was significantly lower than that of ordinary cashmere (17.29 μm).

pmc-12602121.title: Colocalizing Telomeres With PML or γH2AX Foci by IF-FISH in Mouse Brain Neurons
pmc-12602121.creator: Anna Konopka
pmc-12602121.description: Telomere length maintenance is strongly linked to cellular aging, as telomeres progressively shorten with each cell division. This phenomenon is well-documented in mitotic, or dividing, cells. However, neurons are post-mitotic and do not undergo mitosis, meaning they lack the classical mechanisms through which telomere shortening occurs. Despite this, neurons retain telomeres that protect chromosomal ends.

pmc-12610575.title: Transglutaminase Crosslinking Enhances Functional and Structural Properties of Fish Gelatins
pmc-12610575.creator: Sefik Tekle
pmc-12610575.description: Fish gelatins are increasingly recognized as sustainable biopolymers for food, packaging, and biomedical applications; however, their functional performance often requires improvement. In this study, the effects of transglutaminase (TG) modification on the physicochemical and structural properties of trout (T) and sea bass (SB) gelatins were systematically investigated.

pmc-13243181.creator: Xiao Wen, Kong Qingfei
pmc-13243181.description: agues and I read with great interest the retrospective cohort study by Gonzalez et al., which powerfully demonstrates the profound impact of frailty on surgical outcomes across all specialties, particularly in emergent settings [1].
